risks: Low: questions about money can cause embarrassment or distress. Every respondent receives information on the social work service and on travel grants, whatever their score.
consent: Verbal or written consent at the day unit or by telephone, recorded by the coordinator; interpreters used where needed; patients may skip any question.
data: Questionnaires carry a study number; the linkage list for the checkbox analysis is held by the clinical team and destroyed after analysis; no billing or benefit records are accessed.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: younger patients, patients on low incomes, those who stopped working, those living far away and those who speak languages other than English are most affected and least likely to respond. Three modes, four languages, interpreters and weighting are used, and results are reported by these groups.
effectiveness: The survey tells leadership how many patients a navigation service would serve and whether screening would find them.
efficiency: Coordinator time and interpreter funding; no new systems.
costs: Interpreters and translation from budget line SC-2026-11; printing.
grants: None needed; a navigation service could later be evaluated with external funding.
partnerships: Patient and family advisory council, social work, the four day unit managers, and a community organisation supporting patients who travel from rural areas.
rebPath: Approved by the research ethics board on 2026-09-12 (REB-2026-204); any change to the population definition is submitted as an amendment before recruitment.
limitations: Patients who stopped treatment are not reached; self-reported spending; one centre.
summary: Low-risk survey with support information for all, multilingual administration and equity reporting.
